findings: Coverage: 395,352,258 observations → 377,270,972 unique tweets. Full discovery found 3,994,031 hashtag strings; 54,695,204 tweets (14.5%) contain a hashtag. An additional 58 explicit keyword families cover untagged discourse. These are lexical topics, not exhaustive semantic labels for every tweet.

Sentiment: 30,984 unique non-RT posts sampled across 73 candidates; 59 had sufficient common-language strata for adjusted tests, and 15 passed the stated strong-shift rule. Samples are author- and template-capped, not estimates of population sentiment prevalence.
Clearest negative joint signals: PlayStation on Sep 10 (1,451 posts, 5.9× share lift, polarity Δ −0.369); Anthropic on Sep 9 (5,312, 7.9×, −0.210); Manchester United on Aug 22 (70,438, 4.3×, −0.222).

Clearest positive wording shifts: Jungkook on Aug 31 (85,645 posts, 5.0×, Δ +0.443), Michael Jackson on Aug 29 (16,333, 5.4×, +0.347), Bruno Fernandes on Aug 25 (26,072, 7.4×, +0.278), and Kobbie Mainoo on Aug 30 (20,348, 17.8×, +0.249). Birthday/award discourse and fan reactions are visible in supporting posts.
#verzuz on Aug 21 combines an especially sharp attention spike (11,998 posts, 213×) with less-positive wording (Δ −0.182). Its peak mean is approximately neutral (+0.011), not net-negative sentiment.

Large attention does not automatically mean a strong sentiment shift: Dolly Parton discourse reached 274,312 posts on Aug 25 (10.1×); Tim Curry 119,338 on Aug 26 (25.3×); Peter Cullen 58,668 on Aug 27 (22.6×). None passes the predeclared strong-shift rule. Supporting death/mourning claims are corpus content, not independently verified events.

Persistent hashtag volume leaders include #bbnaija, #bb28, #granhermano, and #lacasadelosfamososmx. Fan, quiz, and religious-event campaigns also produce very large hashtag bursts; repeat-template controls often leave too little baseline text for a credible sentiment comparison.

New/sparse-baseline tags are separated from well-supported comparisons. Their enormous smoothed fold changes are not reliable comparative effects. Aug 31 / Sep 1 boundary peaks and unknown collection selection require caution.
trajectories: Anthropic-resignation / AI-safety post 2097476196791709843: +559,845 likes and +147,470,983 recorded views across 196.57 hours, Sep 9–17. Both endpoint values were checked against the original source Parquet. This independently measured growth reinforces the Sep 9 topic/polarity signal; the resignation claim itself is unverified.

Suica campaign post 2097203973975351462: +214,502,814 recorded views and +107,290 likes across 217.56 hours, Sep 8–17. This is attention growth around campaign content, not proof of organic reach or unique viewers. Japanese sentiment is exploratory only.

GPT-6 Astra announcement-like post 2095595741528125780: +129,032,143 recorded views and +279,506 likes across 310.12 hours, Sep 3–16. The topic is a genuine attention candidate, but its sampled polarity does not pass the strong-shift rule. No independent product-release verification was performed.

Borzoi meme post 2097208543333978264: +513,882 likes and +17,209,310 recorded views in 39.31 hours. A strong individual-post growth outlier; the lexical topic has too few sampled peak posts for a strong sentiment comparison.

Shigure Ui × mezzo piano cancellation-notice post 2100493862339047862: +8,681,343 recorded views in 2.274 hours on Sep 17 (3.82 million/hour), plus 5,508 likes. Valid measured intra-day growth, but Sep 17 is partial and excluded from daily peak rankings; Japanese polarity is not treated as validated.

Only 15,134,444 IDs (4.01%) have repeated observations. Most intervals span hours or days, so these are average snapshot-to-snapshot gains. Counter decreases coinciding with blank author/body metadata were verified in source rows and must not be called audience rejection.

topics.entity:playstation: Peak evidence discusses a claimed PHYSINT cancellation/partner switch and explicitly criticizes PlayStation leadership. Sampled wording moves from −0.062 to −0.431. The source also contains unrelated game/console posts; the event claim was not independently verified.
topics.entity:anthropic: AI-safety and resignation discourse. A high-growth post says the author resigned and criticizes Anthropic/OpenAI; sampled wording shifts from −0.152 to −0.362. Whole-post polarity is not a clean measure of opinion toward Anthropic alone.
topics.entity:openai: Overlaps the Anthropic-resignation post and wider AI discussion. Do not add this family to Anthropic counts as if the posts were disjoint.
topics.entity:gpt6-astra: Announcement-like release/rollout discussion. A Sep 3 post gains 129.0M recorded views between snapshots, while the selected daily share peak is Sep 4. Post growth and topic creation-day peaks measure different things. Product claims are unverified.
topics.entity:manchester-united: Aug 22 evidence describes a loss to Hull City and related fan reactions. Wording becomes more negative; this includes both supporters and opposing fans, not a panel of Manchester United supporters.
topics.entity:hull-city: Peak posts describe a win over Manchester United. Strong attention spike (23.7×), but its own sampled polarity does not pass the strong-shift rule. The overlapping Manchester United family does.
topics.entity:jungkook: Birthday/fan discourse is visible around Aug 31 UTC, including a Happy Jung Kook Day post dated 0901. Stronger positive wording survives language adjustment, but this peak lies at the collection-regime boundary.
topics.entity:michael-jackson: Birthday tributes are prominent on Aug 29, alongside unrelated fan discussions. Sampled wording shifts from −0.037 to +0.310; this is a tribute-driven discourse mix, not a change in personal opinion measured longitudinally.
topics.entity:bruno-fernandes: Peak evidence includes a PFA Players’ Player of the Year announcement and fan reactions. Positive wording increases from +0.021 to +0.298. Award claims remain source content, not externally verified facts.
topics.entity:pfa: Award discussion overlaps Bruno Fernandes and other footballers. Large attention lift does not itself imply an equally large sentiment shift in this broader family.
topics.entity:mainoo: Large joint attention/polarity outlier: 17.8× share lift, wording from −0.128 to +0.121. Treat as a change in the mixture of posts mentioning Mainoo, not a direct measure of fan approval.
topics.entity:vmas: Peak posts list nominations; sampled reactions include complaints about omissions and music choices. More-negative wording is consistent with nomination/fandom controversy, not an overall quality rating of the awards.
topics.entity:aew: All In discussion and arrival/return claims dominate high-engagement peak posts. The sample still contains criticism and competing-fandom arguments; the aggregate wording shift is more positive.
topics.entity:gta: GTA VI gameplay/features, anticipation and memes appear at the Aug 27 peak. Wording becomes less negative (−0.201 → −0.017), not strongly net-positive. The lexical family can also match other uses of GTA.
topics.entity:arsenal: Peak posts mix transfer claims and match-day discussion. The wording shift is modestly more positive (−0.132 → +0.028); not evidence that all Arsenal-related events were received favorably.
topics.entity:bbnaija: Peak evidence includes a disqualification claim and fan reactions, alongside other house events. Wording becomes more negative on Sep 7. Repeated fan communities and cohort composition remain important.
topics.entity:ukraine-russia: The Aug 24 sample mixes Independence Day commemoration, conflict news and non-war references such as football. Polarity becomes less negative, but attention lift is only 1.38×. Do not interpret this as improving views of the war.
topics.entity:charlie-kirk: A positive change in score is not positive sentiment: the peak mean remains −0.221 versus −0.429 baseline. Political rhetoric, irony, news and target ambiguity make an approval interpretation unsafe.
topics.entity:tim-curry: High-engagement posts make death claims and include mourning/tribute discourse. Strong attention spike, but raw polarity shift −0.148 narrowly misses the prespecified absolute 0.15 effect-size requirement. Claims were not independently fact-checked.
topics.entity:dolly-parton: A family-message post and mourning/tribute discourse drive attention. Δ −0.142 and adjusted q≈0.058 do not pass the strong-shift rule. Images are not sentiment-scored; the model sees text only. Event claims remain unverified.
topics.entity:peter-cullen: High-engagement posts make death claims and discuss remembered roles. Large attention spike, but no strong sampled polarity shift under the stated rule. Not an independently verified event report.
topics.entity:suica: The largest complete-day lexical share peak is Aug 26, while a separately measured campaign post grows strongly Sep 8–17. These need not be the same event. Japanese-dominated sentiment samples are exploratory.
topics.entity:shigure-mezzo: The complete-day family peak is Aug 23; a cancellation-notice post then shows very rapid measured views growth on partial Sep 17. Do not conflate the two dates or treat Japanese model polarity as validated.
topics.entity:familymart: 10,323 matching posts across the window, but only 19 are non-RT-prefixed. This looks like amplification of campaign text, not 10,323 independent opinions; sentiment evidence is too sparse.
topics.entity:borzoi: A high-growth humorous dog post gained over 513k likes, but only 40 author/template-capped peak posts were available for this lexical family. Individual virality is not sufficient topic-level sentiment evidence.
topics.#verzuz: Event/live-stream discussion mixes enthusiasm, jokes and criticism. The shift is from a positive baseline (+0.194) to an approximately neutral peak (+0.011), not net-negative audience sentiment.
topics.#happyjkday: Birthday campaign tag with a very sharp August share burst. The tag is already positive in its baseline sample and does not itself show a strong additional sentiment shift; the broader Jungkook family does.
topics.#pokemonpersonalityquiz: High-volume sharing of quiz results. Formulaic result text and predominantly unsupported-language evidence limit any sentiment conclusion.
topics.#5dayweekandfairpli: Peak evidence concerns Indian bank employees’ work-week/pay demands. Attention is sharp, but the sampled comparison does not satisfy all support requirements for the strong-shift designation.
topics.#healinggratis: Religious-event/sermon campaign language is visible in supporting posts. A burst of a new slogan is not automatically a change in audience sentiment; template-capped baseline support and common-language sample sizes must be checked.
